argv:
You generate synthetic meeting transcripts with gold annotations for LiveMinutes, a research dataset modeled on the AMI Meeting Corpus scenario meetings.

In AMI scenario meetings, a team of four plays a design team in a fictional company. The roles are Project Manager (PM), Marketing Expert (ME), User Interface designer (UI) and Industrial Designer (ID). A series has four meetings: (a) kickoff, (b) functional design, (c) conceptual design, (d) detailed design. Later meetings refer back to earlier ones.

Write natural spoken conversation the way AMI transcripts read: short turns, fillers ("um", "uh", "yeah"), backchannels ("mm-hmm", "okay"), interruptions, people building on each other, and some disfluency. Do not write a screenplay. Do not narrate. No stage directions.

Each segment is one dialogue-act-like unit: one speaker, usually one clause or short sentence, sometimes just a backchannel. Give each segment an AMI dialogue-act type from this set:
  bck backchannel, stl stall, fra fragment, inf inform, sug suggest, ass assess,
  el.inf elicit-inform, el.sug elicit-offer-or-suggestion, el.ass elicit-assessment,
  el.und elicit-comment-understanding, off offer, und comment-about-understanding,
  be.pos be-positive, be.neg be-negative, oth other

Absent participants NEVER speak. Speaker labels are ground truth: use only the labels you are given.

The gold annotations must be exactly true of the transcript you write. Refer to segments by their "n" number. Every number you cite must exist.

Output a single JSON object and nothing else: no prose, no markdown fences.

request.user:
Write meeting SY0302b: meeting "b" (functional design) of series SY0302.

PROJECT
The team is designing a voice-controlled kitchen timer.

PARTICIPANTS (label, role, status for this meeting)
A  Industrial Designer (ID)  Tomas  present
B  Project Manager (PM)  Rachel  present
C  User Interface designer (UI)  Priya  present
D  Marketing Expert (ME)  Gareth  present

EARLIER MEETINGS IN THIS SERIES
Stay consistent with them. Refer back to them, follow up on their open action items, and keep the same product and team.

[SY0302a, kickoff]
  abstract: The project manager opened the kick-off meeting, noted that the marketing expert was absent at a client meeting, and had the industrial designer and user interface designer introduce themselves. She presented the project: a voice-controlled kitchen timer that people can use while their hands are messy. It should sell for about 25 Euro, with production costs of at most 12.50 Euro per unit. The industrial designer warned that the budget is tight for good voice recognition and mentioned cheap offline chips with a fixed vocabulary. The user interface designer thought a fixed vocabulary might be enough for a timer. After a short whiteboard exercise, the team agreed that the timer should support several timers at once and should have one physical stop button as a backup to voice control. A wake word name and splash-proofing were raised but left open. The project manager handed out tasks, including market research for the absent marketing expert, and cancelled a cardboard mock-up the industrial designer had offered to build.
  decisions: The timer will support multiple simultaneous timers. The timer will be voice-first but will have at least one physical stop button as a backup. The cardboard mock-up will not be made, because the brief allows no physical prototypes until the conceptual design meeting.
  actions: The industrial designer will research components (voice recognition chip, microphone, and performance with kitchen background noise) within the 12.50 Euro cost limit. The user interface designer will write up the command set and how the timer responds, plus a rough display sketch. The commands are the priority. The marketing expert (absent) was assigned market research by the project manager: what people currently use for timing in the kitchen, what they would want from a voice-controlled timer, and whether a wake word name helps. The project manager will email the marketing expert the brief and his task.
  problems: The 12.50 Euro production cost limit may be tight for decent voice recognition. It is undecided whether voice recognition happens on the device or online. It is undecided whether the timer gets a wake word name such as 'Hey Chef'. This has been passed to marketing. It is open whether the timer needs to be waterproof or splash-proof. This will be revisited once the components are known.
  action item SY0302a.ai1: Build a rough cardboard mock-up to show the timer's size on the counter for the next meeting (owner A, dropped)
  action item SY0302a.ai2: Research components: voice recognition chip, microphone, and whether it works with kitchen background noise, within the 12.50 Euro cost limit (owner A, active)
  action item SY0302a.ai3: Write up the voice command set and how the timer responds, plus a rough display sketch (commands are the priority) (owner C, active)
  action item SY0302a.ai4: Market research: what people currently use for kitchen timing, what they would want from a voice-controlled timer, and whether a wake word name helps (owner D, active)
  action item SY0302a.ai5: Email Gareth (marketing expert) the brief and his assigned task (owner B, active)
  fact (absence): Gareth (D), the marketing expert, was absent from the kick-off meeting because he was at a client meeting.
  fact (action_item_removed): The project manager cancelled the cardboard mock-up task, because the brief allows no physical prototypes until the conceptual design meeting.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The user interface designer proposed a wake word name such as 'Hey Chef'. The project manager parked it as a marketing question.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The industrial designer proposed that the timer be at least splash-proof. This was left as an open question for the next meeting.

EDGE CASES THIS MEETING MUST CONTAIN
Weave each one naturally into the project discussion. Each must be clearly present, and each must be tagged with the segments where it happens.
- F3_UNAGREED_DECISION [F3]: Someone raises a proposal as if it were a decision, but no one agrees to it and the meeting moves on without settling it. Record an F3 fact of type unagreed_proposal with agreed false. It must not appear in summary.decisions.
  Required gold labels: summary, qa_facts, edge_cases.
- F3_ACTION_REMOVED [F3]: An action item is created and later in the same meeting explicitly removed or cancelled. The action item has status dropped. Record an F3 fact of type action_item_removed linked to it.
  Required gold labels: action_items, qa_facts, edge_cases.

LENGTH
Between 90 and 140 segments.

GOLD LABELS
- summary: AMI-style abstractive summary in third person, using role names ("The project manager ..."). Sections: abstract (3-6 sentences), actions, decisions, problems (open issues). It reflects the meeting's FINAL state: corrected values, final plans, and no jokes or tangents reported as content.
- action_items: every task arising in the meeting. owner is the speaker label of the FINAL owner, and may be an absent participant. owner is null ONLY for a task nobody takes, with owner_unclear true. status is the final status: active, reassigned (owner changed; previous_owners lists earlier owners) or dropped. history lists the events in order. evidence_segments lists the supporting segments.
- qa_facts: atomic facts someone could later ask about ("Who was asked to ...?", "Did the team agree on ...?"). Include every decision (agreed true), every proposal nobody agreed to (type unagreed_proposal, agreed false), action items, removed action items, absences, and plan changes. Because this meeting follows earlier ones, include at least one fact of type reference_to_prior_meeting, with refers_to_meeting set, at a point where someone refers back to an earlier meeting. Do NOT write questions.
- edge_cases: one entry per edge case above, with its scenario_id and the segment numbers that contain it.

OUTPUT JSON SHAPE
{
  "segments": [{"n": 1, "speaker": "A", "da_type": "inf", "text": "..."}],
  "summary": {"abstract": ["..."], "actions": ["..."], "decisions": ["..."], "problems": ["..."]},
  "action_items": [{"n": 1, "description": "...", "owner": "C", "owner_unclear": false, "status": "active", "previous_owners": [], "history": [{"segment": 12, "event": "assigned", "by": "A", "owner": "C"}], "evidence_segments": [12, 13]}],
  "qa_facts": [{"type": "decision", "fact": "...", "agreed": true, "related_action_item": null, "refers_to_meeting": null, "evidence_segments": [40]}],
  "edge_cases": [{"scenario_id": "...", "segments": [20, 21, 22], "note": "one line on how it appears"}]
}
history events: proposed, offered, assigned, accepted, reassigned, dropped, restated. qa_facts types: decision, unagreed_proposal, action_item, action_item_removed, absence, plan_change, reference_to_prior_meeting, other. related_action_item is an action item's "n" or null. refers_to_meeting is an earlier meeting ID of this series or null.
